definitions.explanation: An older person, typically referring to someone in their senior years. Can sometimes sound slightly informal or even mildly impolite depending on context.

examples.japanese: {年寄|としよ}り⟦には→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{譲|ゆず}りましょう→譲る：02323_yuzuru⟧。
examples.english: Let's give up our seats for elderly people.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{年寄|としよ}り⟦でも→で：00502_de⟧⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather is still energetic despite being elderly.

examples.japanese: {年寄|としよ}り⟦{扱|あつか}い→扱い：12777_atsukai⟧⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please don't treat me like an old person.

examples.japanese: お{年寄|としよ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{優|やさ}しい→優しい：02640_yasashii⟧⟦{町|まち}づくり→町づくり：14151_machizukuri⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{求|もと}められている→求める：02316_motomeru⟧。
examples.english: Creating towns that are friendly to the elderly is called for.

examples.japanese: {年寄|としよ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{知恵|ちえ}→知恵：03428_chie⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦すべきだ→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The wisdom of the elderly should be valued.

notes:
USAGE: {年寄|としよ}り is a common word but can sound somewhat informal or even mildly disrespectful in certain contexts. More polite alternatives exist.

POLITER ALTERNATIVES:
・お{年寄|としよ}り (more polite, with お)
・⟦{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}→高齢者：15649_koureisha⟧ (senior citizen - formal/official)
・⟦{老人|ろうじん}→老人：03784_roujin⟧ (old person - neutral but clinical)
・ご⟦{年配|ねんぱい}→年配：10432_nenpai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧ (elderly person - very polite)
・⟦シニア→シニア：08830_shinia⟧ (senior - loanword)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・お{年寄|としよ}り (elderly people - polite)
・{年寄|としよ}り⟦{臭|くさ}い→臭い：01133_kusai⟧ (old-fashioned, like an old person)
・{年寄|としよ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{冷|ひ}や{水|みず}→冷や水：noentry⟧ (an old person acting young - idiom)

NOTE: Be careful with usage. ⟦{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}→高齢者：15649_koureisha⟧ is preferred in formal or official contexts. お{年寄|としよ}り is acceptable in daily conversation.
